issues.legal_issue: A landlord may use a summary possessory suit to recover property from a trespasser who forcibly dispossessed a tenant in exclusive occupation.
material_facts: The landlord had let the property to a tenant who occupied it and was forcibly dispossessed by third parties.
The landlord brought a suit for recovery of possession against those who had taken possession.
The trial court found that the tenant had been forcibly dispossessed and ordered the defendants to return possession to the landlord.
issues.conclusion: A landlord who retains legal or constructive possession through a tenant may maintain a suit under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 against a trespasser who forcibly dispossesses the tenant, even though the tenant had actual occupation when dispossessed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(1) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 permits a person dispossessed without consent and otherwise than in due course of law, or a person claiming through that person, to sue for possession. Possession includes legal or constructive possession as well as actual physical possession; a landlord retains possession through a tenant, and the tenant's forcible dispossession by a third party also dispossesses the landlord. The Court agreed with Nobin Das v. Kailash Chandra Dey, Ratanlal Ghelabhai v. Amarsing Rupsing, Sailesh Kumar v. Rama Devi, Gobind Ram Jamna Dass v. Mst. Mewa, and Raghuvar Dayal v. Hargovind, and held that Veeraswami Mudali v. P.R. Venkatachala Mudali, (Kanneganti) Ramamanemma v. (Kanneganti) Basavayya, and Ramchandra v. Sambashiv did not state the correct law. The Court's explanation of possession was also informed by Halsbury's Laws of England and Pollock and Wright's An Essay on Possession in the Common Law.

predicates.landlord_bringing_summary_possessory_sui: A landlord brought a summary suit seeking recovery of possession from a person alleged to have taken the property unlawfully.
predicates.landlord_possession_through_tenant: The landlord had let the property to a tenant and retained legal or constructive possession through that tenant.
predicates.tenant_forcibly_dispossessed_by_third_pa: A person other than the landlord forcibly deprived the tenant of occupation without the tenant's consent and otherwise than through legal process.
predicates.landlord_may_recover_possession: The landlord may maintain the summary suit to recover possession from the person who forcibly dispossessed the tenant.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings a summary possessory suit, retains possession through a tenant, and a third party forcibly dispossesses that tenant, the landlord may recover possession.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who was forcibly dispossessed need not be joined as a party to the landlord's summary possessory suit against the trespasser.
material_facts: The landlord sued the persons alleged to have forcibly dispossessed the tenant and sought immediate recovery of the property.
The tenant's dispossession was the basis for the landlord's claim to recover possession.
The issue arose whether the tenant had to be joined in the landlord's suit.
issues.conclusion: The tenant's joinder may be desirable, but the tenant is not invariably a necessary party, and failure to join the tenant does not make the landlord's suit unmaintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 allows a dispossessed person or a person claiming through that person to sue for recovery of possession. A dispossessed tenant may have no interest in pursuing the claim, may be unavailable, or may not wish to litigate. The Court adopted the position in Ratanlal Ghelabhai v. Amarsing Rupsing that a landlord may sue in the landlord's own name for injury to the reversion; the contrary view in (Kanneganti) Ramamanemma v. (Kanneganti) Basavayya and decisions following it was not correct.

predicates.landlord_bringing_summary_possessory_sui: A landlord brought a summary suit seeking recovery of possession from a person alleged to have taken the property unlawfully.
predicates.tenant_forcibly_dispossessed_by_third_pa: A person other than the landlord forcibly deprived the tenant of occupation without the tenant's consent and otherwise than through legal process.
predicates.tenant_not_joined: The landlord did not include the dispossessed tenant as a party to the suit.
predicates.tenant_nonjoinder_does_not_bar_suit: The tenant's absence does not make the landlord's suit unmaintainable, although joining the tenant may be desirable.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings a summary possessory suit after a third party forcibly dispossesses the tenant, the tenant's absence as a party does not bar the suit.
